pass_b_english: …to the sanctified people, obviously through the Spirit, and purified through faith, he fiercely and bitterly attacked, and the Church of God was besieged by the most wicked phalanx of spirits under his hand.
Perhaps he thought he could turn it back, but he was foolish and did not understand anything, for it was not possible for him to capture the holy city of God, the heavenly Jerusalem.

For who can resist the all-powerful God? Therefore, the beast-like enemy has been destroyed along with his own attendants, and he has been driven away from the flock of the pious, as a wild beast leaps upon them.
The Savior taught us, saying: 'Now is the judgment of this world; now the ruler of this world will be cast out. If I am lifted up on the earth, I will draw all to myself' (John 12:31-32).

For the passion of Christ was the overthrow of death, the destruction of the devil, and the abolition of sin, through his being lifted up on the cross and casting down the boast of the devil into the earth.

At the appointed time, God, who is the God of all, introduces the word concerning the birth of the Only-Begotten in the flesh, and reveals the mystery through the voice of prophets, so that having completed the events, he might receive faith from all.
He says: 'Behold, the Lord Sabaoth will shake the glorious ones with power' (Isaiah 13:13).

The mystery of Christ transforms those on earth into a new life of the gospel, as they are turned away from the older customs and from those in shadows and types who no longer have the power to prevail.

But His purpose was to arrive and proclaim, first to the Israelites, that the things lying ahead until the time of correction—that is, the law in the scriptures—will be abolished, transforming the mind of believers into a better and spiritual state.
For all things in Christ are new.

However, although they ought to obey Him, the leaders of the Jewish synagogue and the priests, who did not behave appropriately with the ornaments of holiness, resisted him in a youthful way, acting impiously and wanting to make the mystery of the economy of the Only-Begotten, which had come to them in the flesh, useless by always speaking against the law given through the all-wise Moses.
